title: A job close to home
setting: Lunchtime at the office in late March. Mai (Kimura-san at work) is about to heat up her packed lunch in the kitchenette microwave when her manager, Tanaka-san, comes in with news about his son, who has spent the past year job hunting.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, tanaka-san, otsukaresama desu. saki ni obentou o atatamete mo ii desu ka?
lines.ja: あ、田中さん、お疲れさまです。先にお弁当を温めてもいいですか？
lines.kana: あ、たなかさん、おつかれさまです。さきにおべんとうをあたためてもいいですか？
lines.english: Oh, hi, Tanaka-san. Mind if I heat up my lunch first?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: douzo. a, kimura-san, uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo.
lines.ja: どうぞ。あ、木村さん、うちの息子、やっと仕事が見つかったんですよ。
lines.kana: どうぞ。あ、きむらさん、うちのむすこ、やっとしごとがみつかったんですよ。
lines.english: Go ahead. Oh, Kimura-san, guess what: my son's finally found a job!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: waa, omedetou gozaimasu! kyonen kara zutto shigoto o sagashiteta n desu yo ne.
lines.ja: わあ、おめでとうございます！去年からずっと仕事を探してたんですよね。
lines.kana: わあ、おめでとうございます！きょねんからずっとしごとをさがしてたんですよね。
lines.english: Oh, congratulations! He'd been looking for a job since last year, hadn't he?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee. ichinen mo shigoto sagashite, nakanaka mitsukaranakatta n desu.
lines.ja: ええ。一年も仕事探して、なかなか見つからなかったんです。
lines.kana: ええ。いちねんもしごとさがして、なかなかみつからなかったんです。
lines.english: Yes. A whole year of job hunting, and nothing would turn up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: shigoto ga mitsukatte, honto ni yokatta desu ne. doko no kaisha ni hairu n desu ka?
lines.ja: 仕事が見つかって、ほんとによかったですね。どこの会社に入るんですか？
lines.kana: しごとがみつかって、ほんとによかったですね。どこのかいしゃにはいるんですか？
lines.english: I'm so glad he's found one. Which company is he joining?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sore ga, raigetsu kara, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu.
lines.ja: それが、来月から、うちの会社に入るんです。
lines.kana: それが、らいげつから、うちのかいしゃにはいるんです。
lines.english: Well, that's the thing. Next month he's joining our company.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, kono kaisha ni desu ka? zenzen shirimasen deshita.
lines.ja: え、この会社にですか？全然知りませんでした。
lines.kana: え、このかいしゃにですか？ぜんぜんしりませんでした。
lines.english: What, this company? I had no idea.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: watashi mo kinou made shiranakatta n desu yo. musuko ga jibun de shigoto o sagashite, watashi ni wa nanimo iwanakatta n desu.
lines.ja: 私も昨日まで知らなかったんですよ。息子が自分で仕事を探して、私には何も言わなかったんです。
lines.kana: わたしもきのうまでしらなかったんですよ。むすこがじぶんでしごとをさがして、わたしにはなにもいわなかったんです。
lines.english: Neither did I, until yesterday. He looked for work all on his own and never said a word to me.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sugoi desu ne. musuko-san ga daigaku ni haitta no, kono aida ja nakatta desu ka?
lines.ja: すごいですね。息子さんが大学に入ったの、この間じゃなかったですか？
lines.kana: すごいですね。むすこさんがだいがくにはいったの、このあいだじゃなかったですか？
lines.english: Good for him. Didn't he only just start university the other day?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee, hayai desu ne. demo, daigaku ni haitte kara benkyou bakkari de, shigoto no keiken ga zenzen nai n desu.
lines.ja: ええ、早いですね。でも、大学に入ってから勉強ばっかりで、仕事の経験が全然ないんです。
lines.kana: ええ、はやいですね。でも、だいがくにはいってからべんきょうばっかりで、しごとのけいけんがぜんぜんないんです。
lines.english: Yes, time flies. But since he started university it's been nothing but studying, so he's got no work experience at all.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: daijoubu desu yo. saisho kara keiken ga aru hito wa, hotondo imasen kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫ですよ。最初から経験がある人は、ほとんどいませんから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶですよ。さいしょからけいけんがあるひとは、ほとんどいませんから。
lines.english: He'll be fine. Hardly anyone has experience at the start.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou deshou ka. kimura-san mo, saisho wa keiken ga nakatta n desu ka?
lines.ja: そうでしょうか。木村さんも、最初は経験がなかったんですか？
lines.kana: そうでしょうか。きむらさんも、さいしょはけいけんがなかったんですか？
lines.english: You think so? So you had no experience at first either, Kimura-san?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai. kono kaisha ni haitta toki wa, nanimo dekinakute, mainichi haji o kaite imashita.
lines.ja: はい。この会社に入ったときは、何もできなくて、毎日恥をかいていました。
lines.kana: はい。このかいしゃにはいったときは、なにもできなくて、まいにちはじをかいていました。
lines.english: That's right. When I joined this company I couldn't do a thing, and I was making a fool of myself every day.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou deshita ka? demo ima wa, minna, wakaranai koto wa kimura-san ni kiite imasu yo.
lines.ja: そうでしたか？でも今は、みんな、わからないことは木村さんに聞いていますよ。
lines.kana: そうでしたか？でもいまは、みんな、わからないことはきむらさんにきいていますよ。
lines.english: Were you? Well, these days everyone comes to you when they don't know something.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sonna koto nai desu yo. musuko-san ga komatte itara, watashi mo iroiro oshiemasu ne.
lines.ja: そんなことないですよ。息子さんが困っていたら、私もいろいろ教えますね。
lines.kana: そんなことないですよ。むすこさんがこまっていたら、わたしもいろいろおしえますね。
lines.english: Oh, not really. If your son ever gets stuck, I'll help him out too.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. a, demo, watashi no musuko da tte koto wa, mada minna ni iwanaide kudasai ne.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。あ、でも、私の息子だってことは、まだみんなに言わないでくださいね。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。あ、でも、わたしのむすこだってことは、まだみんなにいわないでくださいね。
lines.english: Thank you. Oh, but please don't tell anyone yet that he's my son.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jibun de haitta kaisha da kara iwanaide tte, musuko ni iwareta n desu.
lines.ja: 自分で入った会社だから言わないでって、息子に言われたんです。
lines.kana: じぶんではいったかいしゃだからいわないでって、むすこにいわれたんです。
lines.english: My son told me not to. He got into this company on his own, he says.

choices.english: Tanaka-san's son is still looking for work after a year, so Tanaka-san asks Mai whether their company might take him on.
Tanaka-san's son has just got into university, and Mai offers to help him get some work experience before he starts.
Tanaka-san's son has finally found a job, at their own company, and Tanaka-san asks Mai to keep quiet for now that he's his son.

questions.explanation: Line 2: uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo. Line 6: the job is at their own company, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu. Lines 16-18: Tanaka-san asks Mai not to tell anyone yet that he's his son, because his son wants it known he got in on his own. A: the son did spend a year looking (line 4), but the search is over. B: university only comes up as Mai remembering when he started (line 9); he's finishing now, and the experience talk is Tanaka-san worrying that he has none (line 10).

questions.english: At Yuki's birthday party, her manager Tanaka-san makes small talk: "What kind of work are you doing at the moment?" Tell him that, actually, you're looking for a job right now.
questions.ja: 今、どんなお仕事をしているんですか？
questions.kana: いま、どんなおしごとをしているんですか？
questions.romaji: ima, donna oshigoto o shite iru n desu ka?
questions.answer: Say you're job hunting with shigoto o sagasu in the -te iru form, politely: jitsu wa, ima shigoto o sagashite iru n desu.

modelAnswers.romaji: jitsu wa, ima shigoto o sagashite iru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: 実は、今仕事を探しているんです。
modelAnswers.english: Actually, I'm looking for a job right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima wa, atarashii shigoto o sagashite imasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 今は、新しい仕事を探しています。
modelAnswers.english: At the moment I'm looking for a new job.

questions.explanation: Looking for work is shigoto o sagasu, and an ongoing search takes -te iru: sagashite iru, or sagashiteru in casual speech. Mai uses it about Tanaka-san's son, kyonen kara zutto shigoto o sagashiteta n desu yo ne (line 3), Tanaka-san adds ichinen mo shigoto sagashite (line 4), and his son found the job jibun de shigoto o sagashite, looking on his own (line 8). Sagasu is only the looking: once the search is over, the job takes ga, shigoto ga mitsukaru.

questions.english: Mai asks you: "Oh yeah, how's the job thing going? Are you still looking?" Tell her no, you've finally found a job.
questions.ja: そういえば、仕事どう？まだ探してるの？
questions.kana: そういえば、しごとどう？まださがしてるの？
questions.romaji: sou ieba, shigoto dou? mada sagashiteru no?
questions.answer: Say the search is over with shigoto ga mitsukaru in the past: uun, yatto shigoto mitsukatta n da!

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, yatto shigoto mitsukatta n da!
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、やっと仕事見つかったんだ！
modelAnswers.english: No, I finally found a job!

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, sengetsu atarashii shigoto ga mitsukatta n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、先月新しい仕事が見つかったんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I found a new job last month.

questions.explanation: Finding work is shigoto ga mitsukaru: the job is what turns up, so it takes ga, not the o of sagasu. Tanaka-san's news is uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo (line 2), and Mai answers shigoto ga mitsukatte, honto ni yokatta desu ne (line 5). Mai's question uses sagasu for the looking; your answer switches both the verb and the particle. Casual speech can drop ga, as in the first model answer.

questions.english: Mai remembers when Tanaka-san's son started university. What did she say?
questions.ja: マイさんは、息子さんについて何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、むすこさんについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, musuko-san ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: that he began university (English 'start' word for word)
that he went to the university

questions.explanation: Mai says musuko-san ga daigaku ni haitta no, kono aida ja nakatta desu ka? (line 9), and Tanaka-san picks it up: daigaku ni haitte kara benkyou bakkari (line 10). You enter a school, so starting university is daigaku ni hairu, the same ni hairu as kaisha ni hairu. B puts English 'start university' into Japanese word for word, and nobody says it. C, daigaku ni itta, means he went there, to the campus or to classes, not that he got in.

questions.english: Tanaka-san's news is that his son will uchi no kaisha ni hairu from next month. What does that mean?
questions.ja: 田中さんの息子さんは、来月から何をしますか？
questions.kana: たなかさんのむすこさんは、らいげつからなにをしますか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san no musuko-san wa, raigetsu kara nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: He'll come into the office with his dad now and then to see what the work is like.
He'll join their company and start working there as a new employee.
He'll take part in a short work-experience event that their company runs.

questions.explanation: Line 6: sore ga, raigetsu kara, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu. Kaisha ni hairu is joining a company as a member of staff: Mai uses it for her own start, kono kaisha ni haitta toki (line 13), and the son wants it known he got in on his own, jibun de haitta kaisha (line 18). Going in to the office is kaisha ni iku or kuru (A), and taking part in an event is sanka suru (C), the word English 'join' tempts you into.

questions.english: Tanaka-san, your manager, asks: "Could I ask you to take on this job? It's a little tricky." Tell him it's fine, because you have experience with this kind of work.
questions.ja: この仕事、お願いしてもいいですか？ちょっと難しいんですけど。
questions.kana: このしごと、おねがいしてもいいですか？ちょっとむずかしいんですけど。
questions.romaji: kono shigoto, onegai shite mo ii desu ka? chotto muzukashii n desu kedo.
questions.answer: Say you have the background with keiken ga aru, politely keiken ga arimasu, not keiken o motte imasu: kou iu shigoto no keiken wa arimasu kara, daijoubu desu.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, kou iu shigoto no keiken wa arimasu kara, daijoubu desu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、こういう仕事の経験はありますから、大丈夫です。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. I've done this kind of work before, so it's fine.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu desu. mae ni mo onaji shigoto o shita keiken ga arimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫です。前にも同じ仕事をした経験があります。
modelAnswers.english: No problem. I've done the same work before.

questions.explanation: Experience is something that exists, so it takes ga aru: keiken ga aru, or keiken ga arimasu to your manager. Tanaka-san worries his son has none, shigoto no keiken ga zenzen nai n desu (line 10); Mai answers saisho kara keiken ga aru hito wa, hotondo imasen (line 11); and Tanaka-san asks her, saisho wa keiken ga nakatta n desu ka? (line 12). Keiken o motte imasu is English 'have experience' word for word and sounds like a line read off a CV. Wa in place of ga (keiken wa arimasu) is fine when you mean this kind of work, at least.
